original_question: Are the deficient enzymes in sialidosis and fucosidosis encoded by genes on the same chromosome?

final_qi.question: Are the deficient enzymes in sialidosis encoded by genes on the same chromosome as those in fucosidosis?
final_qi.long_answer: Sialidosis is caused by a deficiency of the lysosomal enzyme α-N-acetyl-neuraminidase (sialidase) encoded by the NEU1 gene on chromosome 6p21.3. Fucosidosis results from deficiency of lysosomal α-L-fucosidase encoded by the FUCA1 gene on chromosome 1p36.11. Because the responsible genes are located on different chromosomes (chromosome 6 for sialidosis, chromosome 1 for fucosidosis), the deficient enzymes are not encoded on the same chromosome.

final_qi.question: What chromosome is the gene for the deficient enzyme in sialidosis located on?
final_qi.long_answer: Sialidosis is caused by a deficiency of lysosomal α-neuraminidase (encoded by the NEU1 gene). The NEU1 gene is mapped to chromosome 6 at band p21.3; hence, the defective enzyme’s gene in sialidosis resides on chromosome 6.

final_qi.question: What chromosome is the gene for the deficient enzyme in fucosidosis located on?
final_qi.long_answer: Fucosidosis is caused by a deficiency of the lysosomal enzyme α-L-fucosidase. The responsible gene, FUCA1, has been mapped cytogenetically to the short arm of chromosome 1 (region 1p36). Thus, the gene for the deficient enzyme in fucosidosis resides on chromosome 1.
